subject: physiology
title: Principal Cells, Intercalated Cells, and Aldosterone Regulation

steps.tx: The late distal tubule and cortical collecting duct contain two morphologically and functionally distinct cell populations: principal cells and intercalated cells. Comprising over seventy percent of the epithelium, **cortical principal cells** mediate variable sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion under hormonal control.
steps.say: Principal cells reabsorb sodium and secrete potassium under aldosterone control, making up seventy percent of collecting ducts.

left.title: Cortical Principal Cells (~75%)
points: Apical epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) mediate Na+ uptake
Apical ROMK channels mediate potassium secretion
Basolateral mineralocorticoid receptors respond to aldosterone
Apical Aquaporin-2 water channels inserted under ADH stimulation

right.title: Intercalated Cells (~25%)
points: Type A intercalated cells secrete protons and reclaim HCO3-
Type B intercalated cells secrete HCO3- and reclaim protons
Abundant apical and basolateral H+-ATPases and Cl-/HCO3- exchangers
Govern systemic acid-base balance independently of ENaC

steps.tx: Sodium entry across the apical membrane of principal cells is mediated by the **epithelial sodium channel**, universally abbreviated as ENaC. Driven by the chemical gradient maintained by basolateral sodium-potassium ATPases, uncoupled sodium entry creates a transepithelial lumen-negative potential of negative ten to twenty millivolts.
steps.say: Sodium enters principal cells through ENaC channels, creating a lumen-negative voltage that draws potassium out into the urine.

nodes.label: Apical ENaC Channels Facilitate Electro-Diffusion of Sodium into Principal Cells
Uncoupled Cation Reabsorption Generates Lumen-Negative Voltage (-10 to -20 mV)
Electrical Driving Force Pulls Intracellular Potassium into Lumen via ROMK
Basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase Pumps 3 Na+ Out and 2 K+ In, Sustaining the Cycle

steps.tx: Potassium leaves the principal cell through a channel built for quiet, continuous secretion. **ROMK potassium channels** sit in the apical membrane and let potassium follow the electrical gradient created when sodium enters through ENaC. More sodium delivery therefore means more potassium loss, which is why diuretics acting upstream waste potassium. Aldosterone raises channel numbers over hours, tying salt retention firmly to potassium and hydrogen ion excretion.
steps.say: ROMK channels in the apical membrane secrete potassium down the gradient made by sodium entry. More sodium delivery and more aldosterone both increase potassium loss.

vis.alt: Diagram of ROMK potassium channels in the apical membrane of a principal cell, potassium moving into the tubule lumen.
vis.caption: Apical ROMK channels are shown passing potassium from principal cell into the collecting duct lumen. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The lumen-negative transepithelial potential provides the critical electrical driving force for passive potassium secretion across apical **ROMK potassium channels**. Consequently, increased sodium delivery to the collecting duct (such as occurs with loop or thiazide diuretics) accelerates ENaC sodium uptake, enhancing potassium wasting and causing severe hypokalaemia.
steps.say: Increased sodium delivery accelerates ENaC uptake, deepening the negative voltage and causing diuretic-induced potassium wasting.

vis.alt: Distal nephron transport defect and hypokalaemia
vis.caption: Distal nephron electrolyte wasting, potassium secretion mechanics, and hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

steps.tx: The steroid hormone **aldosterone**, synthesized in the adrenal zona glomerulosa, diffuses across the basolateral membrane of principal cells to bind cytosolic mineralocorticoid receptors. The hormone-receptor complex translocates to the nucleus, transcribing serum and glucocorticoid-regulated kinase 1 to stimulate ENaC synthesis and prevent channel retrieval.
steps.say: Aldosterone binds mineralocorticoid receptors, increasing ENaC channel density and driving sodium retention and potassium loss.

vis.caption: Adrenal steroid hormone synthesis, mineralocorticoid receptor dynamics, and renal epithelial target responses.

steps.tx: Pharmacological blockade of aldosterone with spironolactone or eplerenone, or direct ENaC channel blockade with amiloride and triamterene, halts principal cell sodium reabsorption. Known clinically as **potassium-sparing diuretics**, these therapeutic agents abolish the lumen-negative potential, eliminating potassium secretion and effectively preventing or correcting severe diuretic-induced hypokalaemia.
steps.say: Potassium-sparing diuretics block aldosterone or ENaC channels, eliminating the electrical drive for potassium secretion.

left.title: Aldosterone Receptor Antagonists
points: Spironolactone and eplerenone competitive mineralocorticoid blockers
Slow onset of action (requires protein synthesis downregulation)
Indicated in congestive heart failure, cirrhosis, and primary aldosteronism
Risk of hyperkalaemia, especially with ACE inhibitors

right.title: Direct ENaC Blockers
points: Amiloride and triamterene directly plug ENaC pore
Rapid onset independent of gene transcription
Directly eliminates lumen-negative electrical gradient
Specific treatment of Liddle syndrome and lithium nephrogenic DI

steps.tx: Acid excretion in the cortical collecting duct is performed by specialized **type A intercalated cells**. These cells express apical proton-translocating ATPases and apical potassium-proton ATPases, actively pumping hydrogen ions into the tubular lumen against steep hundred-fold concentration gradients while reclaiming filtered potassium.
steps.say: Type A intercalated cells pump protons into urine via apical proton ATPases, regenerating bicarbonate to combat acidosis.

nodes.label: Intracellular CA-II Generates H+ and HCO3- from Cellular CO2 and H2O
Apical H+-ATPase and H+/K+-ATPase Actively Pump H+ into Urine
Luminal H+ Buffered by Ammonia (NH4+) and Titratable Phosphate (H2PO4-)
Basolateral Anion Exchanger (AE1) Returns New HCO3- to Peritubular Blood

steps.tx: Failure of type A intercalated cells to secrete protons into tubular fluid causes **distal type 1 renal tubular acidosis**. Inability to acidify urine below pH five point five results in systemic hyperchloremic non-anion gap metabolic acidosis, accompanied by progressive calcium phosphate nephrolithiasis and severe hypokalemia.
steps.say: Distal type one RTA is the failure of intercalated cells to secrete hydrogen ions, preventing urine acidification below pH five point five.

rows: Type A intercalated cell H+-ATPase failure

steps.tx: Conversely, **type B intercalated cells** operate during systemic metabolic alkalosis to eliminate excess alkali. Featuring a polarity mirror-image of type A cells, they express apical pendrin chloride-bicarbonate exchangers that actively secrete bicarbonate into the lumen while basolateral proton pumps extrude hydrogen ions into the bloodstream.
steps.say: Type B intercalated cells secrete bicarbonate into urine via pendrin exchangers during metabolic alkalosis to restore acid balance.

left.title: Type A Intercalated Cell (Acid Secretor)
points: Activated during systemic acidosis
Apical H+-ATPase and H+/K+-ATPase pumps H+ into lumen
Basolateral AE1 (Band 3) returns HCO3- to systemic blood
Acidifies urine down to a minimum pH of 4.5

right.title: Type B Intercalated Cell (Base Secretor)
points: Activated during systemic metabolic alkalosis
Apical pendrin (Cl-/HCO3- exchanger) secretes HCO3- into urine
Basolateral H+-ATPase pumps protons back into systemic blood
Alkalinizes urine up to pH 8.0 to eliminate excess base
